label: Three provisional photo-backed research-trial character profiles (not official scoring)

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: a small annual with a densely contracted or somewhat interrupted, spike-like panicle, a true short membranous ligule and very short (0–3 mm) lemma awns. Do not use a broken or unexamined floret to choose 'no obvious long awns'; skip that character if damaged. Verify lower 1-veined and upper 3-veined glumes, fertile floret count and actual awn origin before calling the species. Compare other compact pooid grasses.

diagnostic_checks.check: Small tufted annual, culms generally 5–45 cm in GrassBase
Membranous ligule about 1 mm, lacking long hair fringe
Narrow dense to interrupted spike-like panicle approximately 1.5–10 cm in GrassBase
Spikelets approximately 3–7 mm and typically 3–8 fertile florets
Lower glume often 1-veined and shorter, upper glume around 3-veined and broader
Lemma awn may be apical/subapical and short, approximately 0–3 mm

diagnostic_review.unresolved: Actual glume and lemma awn origins, floret counts and ligule unclear; compact spikelike heads resemble other small pooid grasses.

source_notes.unresolved: Actual glume and lemma awn origins, floret counts and ligule unclear; compact spikelike heads resemble other small pooid grasses.
source_notes.field_view: Short cylindrical green bristly panicle with densely overlapping awned or pointed spikelets; small tufted grass.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: numerous short, hairy racemes are borne along a longer central flowering axis; a rooted tuft may have short rhizomes. True inner ligule is an unfringed membrane and fertile lemma awn is often 10–25 mm. Confirm paired sessile/pedicelled spikelets and the translucent line on rachis/pedicel; distinguish angleton bluestem, King Ranch bluestem and other introduced bluestems by actual anatomy, not purple color or general silhouette alone.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: one to six near-terminal/digitate flowering racemes and a bent/twisted fertile lemma awn, often around 10–20 mm. The perennial growth form and true inner ligule are intentionally left unscored here. Compare Bothriochloa bladhii and KR bluestem using sessile/pedicelled spikelets and rachis-pedicel midline; a bare or hairy branch base alone is not an identity test.

Fertile lemma often carries twisted/bent awn roughly 10–20 mm
